# Corpus Mining — Steve Moore, *The Trigrams of Han: Inner Structures of the I Ching* (Aquarian Press, 1989; ISBN 0-85030-808-9, 225 pp.)

Source: `/mnt/agents/upload/_OceanofPDF.com_The_Trigrams_of_Han_-_Steve_Moore.pdf` → `/tmp/moore.txt` (pdftotext -layout).
Moore uses Wade-Giles romanization. Page numbers below are the book's printed page numbers (visible in the layout text).

Scope (Preface, p. 7): "this is not another work on divination … it deals primarily with the eight trigrams and their various arrangements, correspondences and uses, rather than with the hexagrams and texts … a system which sought to explain the nature of the world and its processes in terms of the Five Elements, yang and yin, the directions, numbers, the trigrams and so forth, correlated together like interlocking rings." Central thesis: the correlative system "can be shown to have reached its greatest state of elaboration during the Han dynasty (202 BC–AD 220)" and "there is no evidence of it in the original text of the I Ching itself."

Contents: Part One (1. Basic Groundwork, 2. Historical Context, 3. Web of the World); Part Two (4. World of the Senses, 5. World of Thought, 6. World of the Elements, 7. Three Worlds As One); Part Three (8. Devil Valley Diagram, 9. Eight Arrays); Appendices (1. Ma-wang-tui Sequence, 2. Current Sequence, 3. Worship of T'ai I and the Paces of Yü).

## A. TEXTUAL STRATA (Moore's dating — load-bearing for layer separation)

- Chou I core = Judgements (T'uan) + line judgements only; everything else is later commentary (p. 27).
- **Line texts are older than whole-hexagram judgements** — "reverses the order of the traditional history" (p. 27).
- **Three sources of the line-texts** (p. 27–28): "(1) Peasant omens that we would classify today as 'popular superstition' … some are actually in rhyming verse (e.g. hexagram 31, tinglings in body parts); (2) References to historical figures and events in the late Shang or early Chou dynasties; (3) Simple mantic phrases such as 'Good fortune', 'Perseverance', 'Success' … probably later … added when the divinatory applications … were no longer immediately apparent."
- Dating: written text not before 8th c. BC (Shchutskii, oracle-bone language argument); not reliably attested before late 3rd c. BC; "fixing" of the text most likely Early Han, possibly 136 BC when canonized as a classic (pp. 29–36).
- **Five-line-figure theory** (pp. 33–35): counting-rod arithmetic was base-five; conjectured original figures had FIVE lines (32 variants); 14 hexagrams show the key word in exactly five of six line-places (hexagrams 4, 5, 15, 18, 23, 27(?), 31, 33, 36, 41, 52, 56, 58, 59 — OCR garbled one number, likely 27). A sixth line was interpolated to reach 64. Corollary: "The invention of the trigrams would thus have to date from a period contemporary with, or later than, the construction of the six-line figures" — i.e. **trigrams are NOT necessarily prior to hexagrams**.
- "All the analytic material contained in the commentaries (trigrams, line correspondences, appropriateness of place, 'holding together', and so on) is later than the text itself" (p. 35).
- **Ten Wings** (pp. 42–45): seven texts counted as ten. Group 1 (earlier): T'uan Chuan (2 parts), Hsiang Chuan (= Ta-Hsiang + Hsiao-Hsiang, 2 parts), Ta Chuan/Hsi-Tz'u Chuan (2 parts), Wen Yen (survives only for hexagrams 1–2). Group 2 (later): Hsü Kua Chuan (Sequence), Tsa Kua Chuan (Miscellaneous Notes), Shuo Kua Chuan (Commentary on the Trigrams).
  - Ta Chuan = earliest text using yang/yin as philosophical concepts (p. 43); conjectured 3rd c. BC earliest.
  - T'uan & Hsiang use Five Elements rudimentarily → post-Tsou Yen (after c. 350 BC).
  - **Shuo Kua is the latest commentary and consists of TWO separate texts**: sections 1–3 (a Ma-wang-tui manuscript of exactly these three sections exists → early 2nd c. BC); sections 4–11 "may date even as late as the first century AD" (pp. 44–45).
  - "Only in the latter part of the Shuo Kua Chuan do we find the fully developed system of attributes, arrangements and correlations which form the basic 'structural technology' of the I Ching system" (p. 45).
  - I Wei (Apocrypha; incl. Ch'ien Tso Tu), written after 40 BC (p. 45).

## B. PRIMITIVES

### B1. Yang / Yin (pp. 15–16)
- Relational, not substantial: "we are not talking about two types of physical matter … the 'yang-ness' of one thing by comparison with the 'yin-ness' of another" (p. 15). Sun:yang vs moon:yin; but moon:yang vs stars:yin.
- Reversal rule: "if one principle becomes overly exalted at the expense of the other, it turns into its opposite … Each principle is thus said to contain within itself the 'seed' of the other" (p. 16) — the T'ai Chi diagram.
- Two souls: yang hun (ascends, becomes shen/spirit), yin p'o (earthbound, may become kuei/demon) (p. 16).

### B2. Line types and casting numbers (p. 16–17)
- Yang = unbroken line "known as a light, firm or undivided line"; yin = broken line "dark, yielding or divided line".
- Four casting numbers: **7 = stable yang; 9 = changing yang (turns to yin); 8 = stable yin; 6 = changing yin (turns to yang)**.

### B3. Trigram internal structure (p. 17)
- First line is LOWEST; movement within a trigram (and hexagram) goes bottom→top.
- Line-place ontology: "The lowest line of the trigram is connected with Earth, the second with Man, the third with Heaven" — the San Ts'ai trinity. Heaven round/moving/luminous = yang; Earth square/still/dark = yin; Man the intermediary "having the greatest capacity for direct action" (p. 17).
- Hexagram extension (p. 141): lowest two lines = Earth, lines 3–4 = Man, lines 5–6 = Heaven. Lines 1 and 6 are "outside the action" (before events unfold / after completion). Line 2 = country official; line 3 = transition place where lower meets upper trigram; line 4 = minister; line 5 = king/ruler; line 6 = "outside the action" on exalted scale.

### B4. THE TRIGRAM MASTER ATTRIBUTE LIST (Ch. 1, pp. 17–18) — source: Shuo Kua Chuan
| trigram | Wilhelm name | nature image | quality | family | element |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ch'ien 乾 ☰ | the Creative | Heaven | strong, active | father | Metal |
| K'un 坤 ☷ | the Receptive | Earth | weak, passive | mother | Earth |
| Chen 震 ☳ | the Arousing | Thunder (also earthquake, 'movement within the earth') | movement | eldest son | Wood |
| Sun 巽 ☴ | the Gentle | Wind (also Wood) | penetration | eldest daughter | Wood |
| K'an 坎 ☵ | the Abysmal | Water | danger; the moon | middle son | Water |
| Li 離 ☲ | the Clinging | Fire (also lightning) | —; the sun | middle daughter | Fire |
| Ken 艮 ☶ | Keeping Still | Mountain | — | youngest son | Earth |
| Tui 兌 ☱ | the Joyous | Lake (also mist/clouds) | — | youngest daughter | Metal |

Family-sex derivation rule (p. 18): the lone yang line 'controls' two yin lines and so indicates sex; the POSITION of the odd line gives birth order (1st place = eldest … 3rd place = youngest). (Hatcher gives the same via "two masters one subject = daughter".)

Additional scattered Shuo-Kua attributes Moore cites: Tui = sorceress, lips and tongue (p. 85); Chen = dragon (p. 87); Sun = cock (p. 87); Li = pheasant, weapons/arrows (p. 87); Chen's shape "likened to a bowl" (p. 87); Tui = rain/cloud/mist in World-of-Thought reading (p. 106).

### B5. Five Elements (pp. 18–20)
- Wood, Fire, Earth, Metal, Water (Wu hsing; Moore defends "Elements", suggests "Active Principles").
- **Generation cycle**: Wood→Fire→Earth→Metal→Water→Wood ("Wood generates Fire … Water generates Wood", p. 19).
- **Destruction/Conquest cycle**: Wood conquers Earth, Earth conquers Water, Water conquers Fire, Fire conquers Metal, Metal conquers Wood (p. 20).
- 36 mathematically possible cyclical orders; only Generation and Destruction matter (p. 19).

### B6. Directions + colors + animals (pp. 20–22) — five directions incl. Centre
| direction | element | color | animal |
|---|---|---|---|
| South | Fire | red | Red Bird |
| West | Metal | white | White Tiger |
| North | Water | black | tortoise / tortoise+snake / Dark (Mysterious) Warrior |
| East | Wood | ch'ing (blue-green/'azure') | Azure Dragon |
| Centre | Earth | yellow | (Han: none — iconographic mound; later: ox or yellow dragon) |

Map convention: **South at TOP**; emperor faces South; East on left, West on right (p. 21).

### B7. Ten Celestial Stems (p. 22) — element + direction (Generation order)
1 Chia Wood E; 2 I Wood E; 3 Ping Fire S; 4 Ting Fire S; 5 Wu Earth Centre; 6 Chi Earth Centre; 7 Keng Metal W; 8 Hsin Metal W; 9 Jen Water N; 10 Kuei Water N.

### B8. Twelve Terrestrial Branches (p. 23) — zodiac animal + double-hour
1 Tzu Rat 11pm–1am; 2 Chou Ox 1–3am; 3 Yin Tiger 3–5am; 4 Mao Hare 5–7am; 5 Ch'en Dragon 7–9am; 6 Ssu Snake 9–11am; 7 Wu Horse 11am–1pm; 8 Wei Sheep 1–3pm; 9 Shen Monkey 3–5pm; 10 Yu Cock 5–7pm; 11 Hsü Dog 7–9pm; 12 Hai Boar 9–11pm.
- Sexagenary cycle rule: stems and branches run in parallel; recombine after lcm(10,12)=60 (p. 23).

### B9. Numbers (p. 23)
- All odd numbers yang/Heavenly; all even yin/Earthly. Key numbers: 5 (centre), 9 (highest single yang), 10 (complete cycle). Casting numbers 6,7,8,9 (above). Counting-rod numerals base-five hypothesis links broken/unbroken lines to 5/1 (p. 33).

## C. THE THREE TRIGRAM ARRANGEMENTS (Part Two) — Moore's core contribution

### C1. World of the Senses (= Later Heaven / King Wen arrangement) — Ch. 4
- "certainly the arrangement most commonly mentioned in works of the Han dynasty, if not the only one" (p. 62); appears on a Diviner's Board from a tomb dated AD 68 (p. 62). Referred to by T'uan Chuan directional attributes.
- Positions (compass, S at top): **Chen E, Li S, Tui W, K'an N (cardinal, the Four Cheng 'uprights'); Sun SE, K'un SW, Ch'ien NW, Ken NE (diagonal, the Men 'Gates' or Wei 'Holders Together', per Ch'ien Tso Tu)** (pp. 63, Fig. 4).
- Seasons: Chen spring, Li summer, Tui autumn, K'an winter (p. 64). Ch'ien Tso Tu assigns lunar months: Chen 2nd month, Sun 4th, Li 5th, K'un 6th, Tui 8th, Ch'ien 10th, Ken 12th; each trigram covers 45 days → 360-day lunar year (pp. 64–65).
- Shuo Kua passage (p. 64, §5): "God comes forth in the sign of the Arousing; he brings all things to completion in the sign of the Gentle; he causes creatures to perceive one another in the sign of the Clinging (light); he causes them to serve one another in the sign of the Receptive. He gives them joy in the sign of the Joyous; he battles in the sign of the Creative; he toils in the sign of the Abysmal; he brings them to perfection in the sign of Keeping Still."
- Shuo Kua's own gloss (p. 64): "…the Joyous is midautumn… The Creative is the trigram of the North-West … here the dark and light (yin and yang) arouse each other … The Abysmal … water … due North … toil … Keeping Still is the trigram of the North-East, where beginning and end of all creatures are completed."
- Element attribution to trigrams happens in THIS arrangement (Fig. 5, p. 65): cardinal directions get their proper elements; K'un and Ken both = Earth pushed to SW/NE axis [uncertain: reason for that axis "not immediately apparent" p. 65].
- Moore's mythological decoding (pp. 85–87): western half (Tui, Ch'ien, K'an) = realm of Hsi Wang Mu (Golden Mother, sorceress, K'un-lun mountains, lake where moon rises); eastern half (Chen, Sun, Li) = realm of Tung Wang Kung (Wood Duke, P'eng-lai island, Fu Sang tree, sun rising). Reads clockwise as shorthand myth: "the western lake of heaven from which the moon rises, proceeding toward the mountain (Ken) which lies in the Eastern sea" (p. 86).
- Summary (p. 88): horizontal compass diagram; life-cycles of nature; annual time-progression; arranged round the Lo Shu = circle of Heaven round square Earth; borderland mythical geography; daily motion of sun + monthly motion of moon; shows Generation-cycle influence imperfectly.

### C2. World of Thought (= Earlier Heaven / Fu Hsi / Primal arrangement) — Ch. 5
- Figure 12 layout (S at top): **Ch'ien 1 S (top); Tui 2 SE; Li 3 E; Chen 4 NE; Sun 5 SW; K'an 6 W; Ken 7 NW; K'un 8 N** (numbers run anti-clockwise 1→4 down the left, then clockwise 5→8 up the right; Fig. 20).
- Shuo Kua §3 passage (p. 90): "Heaven and earth determine the direction. The forces of mountain and lake are united. Thunder and wind arouse each other. Water and fire do not combat each other. Thus are the eight trigrams intermingled. Counting that which is going into the past depends on the forward movement. Knowing that which is to come depends on the backward movement. This is why the Book of Changes has backward moving numbers." — pairs are structural opposites (each pair totals 3 yang + 3 yin); pair order in the passage is 1&8, 2&7, 4&5, 3&6 — NOT circular order (p. 90).
- **Binary generation diagram (Shao Yung's school, Fig. 13, pp. 92–93)**: bottom level yang/yin; second level divides → the 'Four Emblems' (四象: == over — etc.); third level divides again → the eight trigrams numbered 1–8 (Ch'ien…K'un). "When this sequence is divided in half and placed in a circle, we have the World of Thought arrangement, and thus the numbering attached to it is explained" (p. 93). A six-level version generates the 64 hexagrams. Moore's dating argument: this division-diagram is Sung (Ch'en T'uan c. 906–989 → Shao Yung 1011–1077); the sequence may have been drawn up to fit the Shuo Kua passage, not vice versa (pp. 91–93). Kuan Lo (AD 209–256) apparently did not know it (p. 63).
- Alternative vertical reading (Fig. 18, pp. 105–106): Ch'ien zenith/Heaven, K'un nadir/Earth; Li (sun) and K'an (moon) move in intermediate space; upper section (Tui=cloud/mist, Ch'ien=heaven, Sun=wind) sky-oriented yang; lower (Ken=mountain, K'un=earth, Chen=earthquake) ground-oriented yin.
- 24-hour reading (Fig. 19, pp. 106–107): facing South, sun moves clockwise: Li E = dawn, Ch'ien top = noon, K'an W = sunset, K'un bottom = midnight; yang lines preponderate in day half, yin in night half.
- Lunar-phase / **Na-chia-type system** (Later Han; correlations "attributed to Ching Fang (77–37 BC)"; found in Ts'an T'ung Ch'i (attr. Wei Po-yang, AD 142) and Yü Fan (AD 164–233)) — pp. 95–97:
  | lunar day | stem | direction | trigram | phase |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 3 | Keng | W | Chen ☳ | 1st appearance (yang enters bottom) |
  | 8 | Ting | S | Tui ☱ | 1st quarter |
  | 15 | Chia | E | Ch'ien ☰ | full |
  | 16 | Hsin | W | Sun ☴ | starts waning |
  | 23 | Ping | S | Ken ☶ | last quarter |
  | 30 | I | E | K'un ☷ | darkness before new moon |
  Li and K'an omitted (their structure can't show a phase); they correspond to Stems Wu/Chi (Centre); "K'an and Wu are said to be the essence of the moon" (p. 97). Order of the six = World of Thought clockwise from Chen.
- Element attribution (Fig. 22, p. 109): assigning elements (Ch'ien/Tui Metal, Li Fire, Chen/Sun Wood, Ken/K'un Earth, K'an Water) and reading 1–8 yields the **Destruction cycle** — symmetric counterpart of the Ho T'u (which holds the Generation cycle).

### C3. World of the Elements (Moore's coined name; Blofeld's "arrangement used in charms") — Ch. 6
- Layout (Fig. 23, S at top): Ch'ien top (S); clockwise: Ken NE→...; order round the circle clockwise from Ch'ien: **Ch'ien, K'an, Chen, K'un, Sun, Li, Tui, Ken** [read from figure; pairs of complementary opposites Ch'ien/K'un and K'an/Li keep World-of-Thought positions; Chen/Sun and Ken/Tui swap] (pp. 110–112).
- Centripetal spiral: one yang line moving down/inward through yin on the right; one yin line through yang on the left; reverse of World of Thought (p. 111).
- Vertical arrangement on the N–S axis (contrast: World of Thought vertical on E–W axis) (p. 112).
- **Familial order = Ma-wang-tui order** (pp. 112–113): clockwise from Ch'ien the trigrams are Ch'ien (father), Ken (3rd son), K'an (2nd son), Chen (1st son), K'un (mother), Tui (3rd dau), Li (2nd dau), Sun (1st dau) — exactly the upper-trigram group order of the MWD manuscript.
- Generation-cycle mapping via Lo Shu numbers read 9→1 (p. 117): Metal 9,8 = Ch'ien,Tui; Water 7 = K'an; Wood 6,4 = Chen,Sun; Fire 3 = Li; Earth 2,1 = Ken,K'un. (5 = centre, no trigram.) Symmetry 2-1-2-1-2 pivoting on centre.
- Moore's hypothesis (pp. 118–119): this may be the EARLIEST arrangement; both the element attributions and the familial attributes may have originated here, later absorbed illogically into the World of the Senses.

### C4. Lo Shu trigram-number assignment (from T'ai I circulation, App. 3, p. 200)
T'ai I's yearly circuit through the Nine Palaces (Ch'ien Tso Tu): 1st North = **K'an=1**, 2nd SW = **K'un=2**, 3rd East = **Chen=3**, 4th SE = **Sun=4**, 5th Centre (rest), 6th NW = **Ch'ien=6**, 7th West = **Tui=7**, 8th NE = **Ken=8**, 9th South = **Li=9** — following the magic line of three; every line of the square sums to 15. Quote: "The yang in operating advances, changing from 7 to 9 … The yin in operating withdraws, changing from 8 to 6 … the Supreme One (Tai I) takes these (yin and yang) numbers as it circulates among the nine halls … (The numbers of the trigrams) in every case add up to 15" (pp. 199–200). — This is the standard Later-Heaven Lo Shu trigram mapping (gold for number maps).

## D. PART THREE DEVICES

### D1. Devil Valley Diagram (Ch. 8) — six concentric rings read as a hexagram
Ring↔line mapping (pp. 141–143): Ring 1 (Earth, trigram-line 1 / hexagram-lines 1-2): Generation cycle simple form + directions. Ring 2: Celestial Stems (human invention defining Earth's directions; hexagram line 2 = country official). Ring 3 (trigram-Heaven / hexagram-Man): the eight trigrams — "no better symbol of transition and mutation" (p. 142). Ring 4: numbers (divided by sex odd/even; familial designations; line 4 = minister). Ring 5 (king/ruler, first line of Heaven): Eight Gates + Ch'i-men Tun-chia divination + war + Terrestrial Branches. Ring 6 (Heaven, 'outside the action'): Generation cycle on cosmic scale, symbolic animals as constellations, astrology.
Three zones: Earth (rings 1–2: generation cycle + directions), Man (rings 3–4: change + mathematics — "measuring the Earth and imposing order on the world by number"), Heaven (rings 5–6: warfare, magic, divination, astrology) (p. 143).

### D2. THE EIGHT GATES MASTER TABLE (Ch. 9, p. 165) — gates ↔ trigrams ↔ directions ↔ array names
| class | array name | trigram | direction | gate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Men (diagonal) | HEAVEN | Ch'ien | North-West | Gate of Opening (K'ai) |
| Men | EARTH | K'un | South-West | Gate of Death (Ssu) |
| Men | WIND | Sun | South-East | Gate of Obstruction (Tu) |
| Men | CLOUD | Ken | North-East | Gate of Life (Sheng) |
| Cheng (cardinal) | BIRD | Li | South | Gate of Prospect (Ching) |
| Cheng | SERPENT | K'an | North | Gate of Rest (Hsiu) |
| Cheng | DRAGON | Chen | East | Gate of Injury (Shang) |
| Cheng | TIGER | Tui | West | Gate of Surprise (Ching/Alarm) |
Gate order in the Devil Valley Diagram runs clockwise from North (pp. 161, 165). Names from Wu Pei Chih (AD 1628); gates = World of the Senses trigrams "in an amplified form" including divination, ritual magic, military strategy (p. 4890s region / Ch. 9). [Gate-name romanizations: Moore gives English only; Chinese names are the standard Ch'i-men Tun-chia set — inferred.]

## E. HEXAGRAM SEQUENCES (Appendices)

### E1. Ma-wang-tui sequence rules (App. 1, pp. 185–187)
- 8 groups of 8 by UPPER trigram, ordered by sex: male group Ch'ien(father), Ken(3rd son), K'an(2nd son), Chen(1st son); female group K'un(mother), Tui(3rd dau), Li(2nd dau), Sun(1st dau).
- LOWER trigram order within a group: Ch'ien, K'un, Ken, Tui, K'an, Li, Chen, Sun (alternating sex); each group STARTS with the doubled trigram (Ch'ien/Ch'ien first of group 1, Ken/Ken first of group 2 …), then follows the lower-trigram order.
- Full MWD→current-number mapping (Fig. 42): group rows:
  1–8: (1)(12)(33)(10)(6)(13)(25)(44)
  9–16: (52)(26)(23)(41)(4)(22)(27)(18)
  17–24: (29)(5)(8)(39)(60)(63)(3)(48)
  25–32: (51)(34)(16)(62)(54)(40)(55)(32)
  33–40: (2)(11)(15)(19)(7)(36)(24)(46)
  41–48: (58)(43)(45)(31)(47)(49)(17)(28)
  49–56: (30)(14)(35)(56)(38)(64)(21)(50)
  57–64: (57)(9)(20)(53)(61)(59)(37)(42)

### E2. Current (King Wen) sequence rules (App. 2, pp. 189–198)
- Pair rule: "The second [hexagram] of each pair is the inverse of the first"; 4 exceptional pairs are OPPOSITE (not invertible): 1&2, 27&28, 29&30, 61&62; 4 pairs are both opposite and inverse: pairs 6, 9, 27, 32 (i.e. hex pairs 11&12, 17&18, 53&54, 63&64) (p. 190).
- Yin/yang alternation of pair positions: even pair positions tend to hold yin-preponderant hexagrams, odd positions yang-preponderant; 10 pairs are even 3yang/3yin splits (pairs 6,9,11,16,21,24,27,28,30,31) (p. 190).
- Rising/falling pattern: minority lines rise upward from first to second hexagram of a pair, or fall (Fig. 43 labels pairs: Opposite/Even/Rising/Falling × Yang/Yin) (pp. 190–191).
- Moore's reconstruction: original book likely two equal halves of 32; opposite pairs would sit at positions 1, 16, 17, 32; current order corrupted by later transpositions (pp. 192–198) [speculative, Moore's own].

## F. COSMOLOGICAL OPERATING PRINCIPLES (Ch. 3 "Web of the World")
- Resonance: microcosms (Ming T'ang, maps, diviner's board, trigram circles) are "linked by resonance to the world at large … not a simple 'artistic symbol' but something that has an active use" (p. 55). Wang Mang anecdote: seated with Diviner's Board (square Earth plate + rotating round Heaven plate marked with Dipper; Earth plate inscribed with Stems and Branches), aligning with day/hour (pp. 55–56).
- Ming T'ang numerology (Po Hu T'ung, p. 54): "round at the top, and square at the bottom … eight windows represent the Eight Winds, the four doors the four Seasons, the nine compartments the Nine Provinces, the 12 seats the Twelve Months, the 36 single doors the Thirty-six Rains, the 72 window-openings the Seventy-two Winds."
- Time is circular, not linear (p. 48). Elements are processes with two aspects (each generates one and conquers one) → self-balancing system (p. 49).
- Season-element problem: 5 elements vs 4 seasons; Earth given either late-summer or four 18-day intercalary periods between 72-day seasons ≈ 360-day year (p. 49).
- Trigram extensions: "correlated with the Eight Winds, the eight types of instrumental music, the eight parts of the body, and so on" (p. 56) — Moore does NOT tabulate these [gap].
- Diviner's board archaeology: World-of-Senses sequence on board from AD 68 tomb (p. 62).

## G. RULES EXTRACTED (numbered)
1. R-M1 Combination: trigram × trigram → hexagram (doubling; lower=Zhen/inner, upper=Hui/outer; Moore discusses attribution to King Wen as fiction but uses the structure).
2. R-M2 Line build order: hexagram grows bottom (line 1) → top (line 6); same for trigram.
3. R-M3 Change operator: 9→8 (old yang becomes yin), 6→7 (old yin becomes yang); 7,8 stable.
4. R-M4 Generation cycle: Wood→Fire→Earth→Metal→Water→(Wood).
5. R-M5 Destruction cycle: Wood⊣Earth, Earth⊣Water, Water⊣Fire, Fire⊣Metal, Metal⊣Wood.
6. R-M6 Sex/birth-order from line pattern: odd-line-out determines sex; its position (1/2/3) determines seniority (eldest/middle/youngest).
7. R-M7 Three Powers placement: trigram lines = Earth/Man/Heaven bottom→top; hexagram = EE MM HH in line pairs.
8. R-M8 Sexagenary enumeration: stems ∥ branches, lcm=60.
9. R-M9 Resonance principle: symbolically correct configuration affects the world laterally ("operations can be carried out by the manipulation of symbols to produce effects laterally through the connected web of correlations and resonances", p. 161).
10. R-M10 MWD sequence generation (familial upper groups × alternating lower cycle, doubled trigram first).
11. R-M11 Current-sequence pairing (inverse pairs; opposite when self-inverse) + yin/yang position polarity + rising/falling minority lines.
12. R-M12 T'ai I circulation = Lo Shu magic line order over 8 trigrams + centre (nine palaces).
13. R-M13 Lunar najia (Later Han): 6 trigrams ↔ stems ↔ directions ↔ moon phases (table C2); Li/K'an → Wu/Chi → centre.
14. R-M14 Devil Valley diagram = hexagram-analogue ring assignment (6 rings ↔ 6 lines ↔ 3 powers).
15. R-M15 Polarity reversal at extremes: "when the yang reaches excess, it turns into yin, and vice-versa" (p. 16).

## H. CANDIDATE DIMENSION ATTRIBUTION (project dims: Movement=vectors/where; Evolution=becoming/when; Being=state/quality; Design=structure/form; Space=container/resonance)
- Yang/yin pair, line types, 6/7/8/9 casting → **Being** (state/quality primitives) with a transition operator (Evolution) attached to 6/9.
- Three Powers (Earth/Man/Heaven), line-place ranks (official…king, 'outside the action') → **Design** (positional structure/form) — Moore explicitly treats place as structural technology.
- Directions, compass degrees, gates, stems/branches-as-directions → **Movement** (where/vectors). Note gates are literally thresholds of motion (army enters/exits).
- Seasons, months, lunar phases, 24-hour sun reading, T'ai I yearly circuit, sexagenary calendar → **Evolution** (becoming/when).
- Five Elements as "processes" straddle **Evolution** (generation/destruction = transformation rules) and **Being** (as substantive qualities/colors/tastes).
- Trigram nature-images (heaven/earth/thunder/wind/water/fire/mountain/lake) + family + body + animal → **Being** (state/quality vocab).
- The three circular arrangements themselves + Lo Shu/Ho T'u + Devil Valley rings + MWD/King-Wen sequence algorithms → **Design** (formal structure).
- Resonance principle, microcosms (Ming T'ang, diviner's board, arrays as stones), "connected web" → **Space** (container/resonance) — Moore's whole ch. 3 is about containment-and-resonance coupling.

## I. NOTABLE GAPS in Moore
- No full Shuogua extended lists (animals/body per trigram) — only scattered mentions (cited above).
- No Najia line-by-line stem assignment to hexagram lines (only the 6-trigram lunar-stem system).
- No Eight Palaces (pa kung) hexagram-generation system.
- No compass-degree numbers (no 24-mountain/degree table).
